description: Deterministic technique DAG for autoregressive LLM serving. Traversed greedily by a state machine: apply a node, measure, keep or revert, follow the corresponding edge. Every measurement is recorded as a Pareto candidate whether or not it becomes the incumbent.

inputs.incumbent_config: best config from stage 1.2, validated by 1.3
inputs.incumbent_metrics: measured goodput / ttft_p99 / itl_p99 / quality at stage 1.3
inputs.accept_band: Relative improvement required to keep a node. Sourced from the calibration store for this (model, hardware) pair; falls back to a deliberately LOOSE default when the pair has never been measured. Never hardcoded in a node, and the run report states which of the two it used -- a result should never rest silently on a default.
inputs.fingerprint: model / hardware / workload characterization from stage 0, including a lora block: n_adapters, max_rank, target_modules, request_distribution, adapter_switching_rate.
inputs.slo: user TTFT and ITL constraints; violated configs score goodput 0
inputs.quality_budget: user allow-loss, or null to produce the frontier and let them pick
inputs.quality_tolerance: Per-benchmark score delta that counts as noise. Measured at lossless_complete and written back to the calibration store; a per-benchmark default until then.

objective.definition: throughput counting only requests that satisfy the SLO constraints

traversal.decision_rule: keep the best swept variant if goodput > incumbent.goodput * (1 + accept_band) and it satisfies every constraint; otherwise revert
traversal.revert_semantics: reverting discards the node's effect on the incumbent, NOT its measurements. A reverted config is still a Pareto candidate and may be the operating point the user wants.

budget_guard.on_exceed: stop traversal, emit the frontier from what was measured, list unvisited nodes
budget_guard.note: Raised from 20/26 when max_num_batched_tokens added two launches. The guard is a backstop against a DAG that cannot finish, not a target -- graph_capture's hint also dropped 40 -> 9 after measurement, so the minute estimate fell by ~31.

traversal.skip_semantics: A node is not executed when status != 'active' OR applicable_when evaluates false. In both cases the traverser follows its on_keep edge straight through. This keeps TODO and inapplicable nodes wired into the spine so enabling one is a predicate or status change, not a rewiring.

equivalence.note: greedy generations compared against the incumbent's. Detects an accidentally-lossy change without paying for a benchmark.

quality.finalist_set: full public dataset, or 1000+ if the user supplies a custom eval set
quality.report: point estimate with confidence interval; state the resolution the sample size buys

benchmarks.scoring: test execution in a subprocess (mbpp_score.py), greedy decode, chat template with thinking disabled
benchmarks.why: code breaks on a single wrong token - highest sensitivity per sample to quantization damage. MBPP+ adds ~35x the test cases of original MBPP, so a solution that only fits the example assertion is caught.
benchmarks.contamination_note: MBPP predates the models under test and is likely in pretraining data. That does not matter here: every row of the frontier is the SAME model against ITSELF under different serving configs, so a memorised problem is memorised equally on both sides and cancels. Contamination would only matter for an absolute claim about the model's coding ability.
benchmarks.sandbox: evalplus rlimits + signal timeouts in a separate process. Guards against runaway generated code, NOT against an adversary. Run mbpp_score.py inside a container if that changes.

benchmarks.why: code breaks on a single wrong token - highest sensitivity per sample to quantization damage
benchmarks.status: NOT WIRED. No longer blocked on a sandbox -- mbpp_score.py is one, and evalplus serves HumanEval+ from the same API. Unregistered because mbpp_plus already covers this axis and a second code benchmark costs a full ladder of GPU time to repeat it.

benchmarks.why: long reasoning chains, genuine headroom at 9B scale

nodes.title: Stage 1 result
nodes.note: No work. The predictor's config, already measured twice in stage 1.3. Parallelism, CUDA graphs, KV fraction and max token capacity were decided there and are deliberately NOT revisited here - AIConfigurator models them, this DAG does not. When fingerprint.lora.n_adapters <= 1 every LoRA node below evaluates its predicate false and the traverser falls straight through to max_model_len_rightsize at zero cost.

nodes.title: Multi-LoRA vs merged replicas
nodes.rationale: N merged replicas cost N x weight memory but delete every LoRA kernel AND restore a valid performance predictor per model. For small N on a small model that can beat 1 base + N adapters outright. Only offered when the replicas actually fit.

nodes.title: Right-size max LoRA rank
nodes.rationale: Rank buffers are allocated to the declared maximum. Declaring 64 when every adapter is rank 8 wastes memory that KV blocks could use. Same shape of win as right-sizing the context window.

nodes.title: Adapters resident per batch
nodes.rationale: How many distinct adapters a single batch may mix. Higher means requests for different adapters batch together instead of serializing; it also costs memory. The right value follows the request distribution, so sweep around it rather than guessing.

nodes.title: CPU-side adapter cache
nodes.rationale: Adapters not resident on GPU are swapped in on demand. A CPU cache turns a cold-adapter request from a disk read into a host-to-device copy. Only matters when there are more adapters than GPU slots.

nodes.title: Prefix caching
nodes.rationale: Placed FIRST among the flag nodes, ahead of the batching and context nodes. On a workload with real prefix sharing this is what makes the SLO reachable at all: measured 2368ms -> 630ms TTFT and 15% -> 97% attainment on Qwen3-14B/GB10. Until attainment is high, goodput is quantised by whole requests -- at 15% attainment one request flipping moves goodput ~11%, against a 5% accept band -- so every node judged before it is decided on noise. The SLO-enabling technique has to come before the nodes measured against the SLO.

nodes.title: Right-size the context window
nodes.rationale: Every unused position of context costs KV blocks that could hold real sequences. Cheapest structural win in the tree and routinely left on the table.

nodes.title: Chunked prefill
nodes.rationale: Interleaves prefill with decode, trading TTFT against ITL. Only meaningful when prompts are long enough for prefill to block decode.
nodes.sweep_note: bracketed: 3rd interior point cost a launch and rarely moved the decision
nodes.curve_note: Negative at low concurrency -- chunking a prefill that could run in one shot is pure overhead -- and positive at high concurrency, where it stops a long prefill blocking every decode behind it. The curves cross, so a single-point measurement is a coin flip.

nodes.title: Scheduler token budget per step
nodes.rationale: The number of tokens the scheduler may put in one forward pass, and the chunk size chunked_prefill actually uses -- the two are the same knob seen from different ends, which is why this sits next to it. vLLM's own auto_tune sweeps exactly this alongside max_num_seqs, and it was absent here entirely, so half of what the reference tool tunes was never touched. Gated on p99 input > 512 because below that a prefill fits in any budget and the knob does nothing.
nodes.curve_note: Crosses. A large budget lets one long prefill monopolise a step, which raises throughput at high concurrency and pushes TTFT out at low concurrency; a small budget does the reverse. Scored on its peak across the bracket, like the other crossing families.
nodes.sweep_note: Values taken from vLLM's benchmarks/auto_tune ranges rather than invented, so a result here is comparable to that tool's.

nodes.title: KV block size
nodes.rationale: Larger blocks cut paging overhead but coarsen allocation and waste tail memory. Only matters once sequences are long.

nodes.title: Speculative decoding, n-gram proposer
nodes.rationale: Rejection sampling preserves the target distribution, so this is distributionally lossless. Needs no draft model. Helps decode only - pointless on prefill-dominated traffic. Gated on mean OUTPUT LENGTH rather than the decode token fraction: the token ratio understates decode's share of wall clock by roughly two orders of magnitude, so a 0.4 token-ratio threshold would exclude workloads that are overwhelmingly decode-bound in time.
nodes.curve_note: Speculative decoding spends spare compute to amortise weight reads. At low concurrency there is spare compute and it wins; at high concurrency weight reads are already amortised across sequences and rejected drafts are pure waste, so it can go negative. Mirror image of chunked_prefill.

nodes.title: Speculative decoding, draft model
nodes.rationale: Reached only when n-gram acceptance was poor. Gated off under multi-LoRA: the draft must approximate the ADAPTED target, so acceptance collapses against a domain-adapted model and you would need one draft per adapter. n-gram is unaffected because it never models the network at all. Valid again once merged.
nodes.todo: Requires a draft-model registry per target model. Deferred with NVFP4.

nodes.title: Speculative depth refinement
nodes.rationale: Acceptance rate and optimal depth trade off directly: deeper speculation wins more per hit and wastes more per miss. Refine only after a proposer has proven itself.
nodes.curve_note: Same crossing behaviour as the proposer it depends on.

nodes.title: CUDA graphs / torch.compile
nodes.rationale: Deliberately LAST in the lossless branch and deliberately its own node. Compilation is expensive (~30 min on GB10) and keyed on shapes, so a cache warmed at one max_num_seqs is invalidated by the next sweep value -- paying it per node would cost more than the whole search. Every earlier node runs eager, then this one tests compilation ONCE against the config they accumulated. It also belongs here for a second reason: the compile is worth most on the final shapes, not on shapes that are about to change.
nodes.cost_note: ~9 min measured on GB10/Qwen3-14B across runs 4, 7 and 9. Was 40, carried over from a different model on different hardware and never re-checked.

nodes.title: Lossless frontier checkpoint
nodes.note:
Emit the lossless frontier before entering the lossy branch -- if the budget guard fires, the run still delivers a complete result here.

ALSO measures the quality tolerance, for free in the useful sense: lossless nodes cannot move quality by definition, so the difference between quality here and quality at stage 1.3 IS the noise, and it spans the whole lossless traversal -- every launch, config change and thermal state in between, which is exactly the variation the lossy gate has to survive. A dedicated repeat would measure less.

Budgeted at 1 launch conservatively. When the preceding node was KEPT, the live server already holds the incumbent config and the probe is free; only a REVERTED predecessor requires a relaunch, since its server holds a rejected config rather than the incumbent.
nodes.on_measure: If the quality delta exceeds what per_token_flip_rate predicts, something in the lossless branch was not lossless. Stop and report rather than entering the lossy branch on a corrupted incumbent.
quality_benchmarks_todo: mbpp_plus is wired and executes in a sandbox (mbpp_score.py); humaneval_plus remains unregistered by choice, not by blocker

nodes.title: FP8 KV cache
nodes.rationale: Entered first in the lossy branch because it has the best gain-to-damage ratio: roughly halves KV memory, touches no weights, and the damage is concentrated in long-context recall. NOTE: no active benchmark probes that axis since ruler_multineedle was removed, so this node's quality gate is weaker than it looks -- MATH-500 will not see long-context degradation.
nodes.lora_caveat: Under multi-LoRA the quality probe must run WITH adapters applied and with a request mix matching fingerprint.lora.request_distribution. A published base-model quantization benchmark understates the damage: the adapter was trained against unquantized weights, so it is correcting for weights that no longer exist. Verify the runtime supports quantized base + LoRA for this format before trusting the node at all.

nodes.title: Re-tune batching after freeing KV memory
nodes.rationale: THE interaction node. Halving KV memory changes where batching saturates, so the concurrency chosen in stage 1 is now wrong. This is a distinct forward node, not a back-edge - the graph stays acyclic and the state machine stays deterministic.

nodes.title: Un-merge to reach published quantized checkpoints
nodes.applicable_when: preconditions.merge_verification.merged and fingerprint.lora.adapter_retained and (fingerprint.model.can_quantize_fp8 or fingerprint.model.can_quantize_int4_awq)
nodes.rationale: Two reasons, and the first is structural rather than about quality. (1) v1 quantizes only from PUBLISHED checkpoints, and those are of the original base model -- once an adapter is merged the served weights match no published checkpoint, so the entire weight-quantization branch becomes unreachable without calibration. Serving unmerged over a published quantized base restores it. (2) It is also the arrangement where a BF16 adapter sits above quantized weights and can partially compensate for quantization error, which is the QLoRA serving shape. The merge gate in stage 0 was decided at BF16 and cannot see either effect.
nodes.cost_note: 1 launch, not 2 -- the merged arm was already measured by the incumbent at this point in the traversal, so only the alternative needs running.
nodes.revert_note: Reverting means staying merged, which leaves no published checkpoint to quantize from. The lossy branch ends here with KV quantization already applied; weight quantization needs the calibration pipeline (see future.conversion_pipeline).
quality_benchmarks_todo: mbpp_plus is wired and executes in a sandbox (mbpp_score.py); humaneval_plus remains unregistered by choice, not by blocker

nodes.title: Weight quantization: AutoQuantize search plus fixed-format references
nodes.rationale: Replaces three separate single-format nodes (fp8, int4_awq, nvfp4) with one search over a BIT BUDGET. NVIDIA's AutoQuantize scores each layer's sensitivity -- KL divergence between unquantized and quantized outputs -- then solves a constrained assignment for a per-layer format: FP8 where it matters, NVFP4 where it does not, skipped where nothing survives. Fully deterministic: same model, same calibration data, same effective_bits gives the same checkpoint. It also answers 'which layers to protect' by measurement, replacing a hand-picked ignore list that was never validated.
nodes.constraint: Produced LOCALLY from the served checkpoint, calibrated on the user's own trace. Never a published quantized repo: the customer's model has none, and measuring someone else's would benchmark their calibration job.
nodes.sweep_note:
Two bit budgets and two fixed formats, measured the same way.

The budgets are what AutoQuantize searches: effective_bits 6.0 is roughly FP8-with-headroom, 4.5 roughly NVFP4-with-protected-layers. Each is a distinct point on the size/quality curve.

int4 (W4A16_NVFP4) and nvfp4 are whole-model single formats and are here as REFERENCES, not as candidates in their own right. AutoQuantize assigns per layer across these same formats, so it should beat both -- and if it does not, that is worth knowing, because it means the sensitivity scoring is not paying for its cost on this model. A search you never compare against the thing it replaced is a search you cannot evaluate.

Every point is MEASURED on goodput AND on the eval set. AutoQuantize optimises an internal sensitivity proxy; it cannot know whether the result helps goodput at this SLO or survives MATH-500.
nodes.quality_note: MANDATORY. Quality on the eval set is the only thing that says whether a quantization did a good job -- goodput alone would keep a checkpoint that serves twice as fast and cannot do arithmetic. Measured against the tolerance established at lossless_complete, so a drop inside the eval's own resolution limit is not mistaken for damage.
nodes.cost_note: Four conversions, four launches, four quality probes. The conversion dominates: AutoQuantize scores sensitivity with a forward pass per candidate format before calibrating the chosen assignment, so a budget point costs more than a fixed-format one. Roughly 45-80 min each on a 14B model.
nodes.format_note:
w4a16 is W4A16_NVFP4_CFG: 4-bit FLOAT weights (NVFP4) with 16-bit activations. nvfp4 is NVFP4_DEFAULT_CFG: 4-bit weights AND activations. The pair brackets how aggressive to be about activations, which is where quality usually goes first.

True INT4-AWQ is unavailable. INT4_AWQ_CFG emits quant_algo W4A16_AWQ and vLLM's modelopt loader accepts only FP8, FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN, FP8_PB_WO, NVFP4, W4A16_NVFP4, MXFP8 and MIXED_PRECISION. Found by producing the checkpoint and watching vLLM refuse it -- both surviving 4-bit paths are verified to load and generate. AutoQuantize emits MIXED_PRECISION, which is on the list.
nodes.bits_note: The achievable effective_bits FLOOR is model-dependent, so these values may be infeasible on some models. modelopt never quantizes embeddings, lm_head, routers or vision towers, and the floor is set by what fraction of parameters those are: ~21% on Qwen3-0.6B gives a floor of 7.5 bits, ~5% on a 14B gives roughly 4.6. An infeasible budget fails with the actual floor named rather than a stack trace.

nodes.title: Re-tune batching after weight quantization
nodes.rationale: Second interaction node, same reason as the first: quantized weights free memory and shift the arithmetic intensity, so the batching optimum moves again.

nodes.title: Emit the Pareto frontier
nodes.note: Compute the true non-dominated set over (quality, goodput, ttft_p99, memory_gb) across EVERY measurement taken, including reverted ones. Re-run quality on the 2-3 frontier candidates against the full benchmark sets, report with confidence intervals, and hand the user the operating points.

stage_3_gepa_nodes: custom kernel generation for an operator the profiler flags as dominant
admission control and queueing policy as a written program rather than a flag
replacing applicable_when predicates with a reasoner that reads diagnostics and skips nodes the profile says cannot help - measurable as: same frontier, fewer launches
future.conversion_pipeline: baseline -> FP8 / INT4 / NVFP4 for customer-supplied models, offline, outside the 2-3h budget

preconditions.lora_single_adapter_is_merged_upstream:
When fingerprint.lora.n_adapters == 1, stage 0 merges the adapter into the base weights before stage 1.2, because the merged model is architecturally identical to the base -- same GEMM shapes, no SGMV kernels -- which makes the performance predictor valid again and removes LoRA from the serving path entirely.

EQUIVALENCE CLASS: quality-equivalent (VERIFY), not strictly equivalent. (W0 + BA)x == W0x + BAx holds algebraically (LoRA, arXiv 2106.09685), but the merged weights are rounded back to the storage dtype on save while the unmerged path accumulates separately, so outputs are NOT bitwise identical. No paper establishes identical held-out task performance for single-adapter merge; the merge literature (TIES/DARE-TIES, LoRI, Compress-then-Merge) studies merging MULTIPLE adapters together, which is a different and demonstrably lossy operation. Merging into a QUANTIZED base is separately lossy -- W0+BA cannot be represented in the quantized format without a second re-quantization step.

Therefore stage 0 must VERIFY the merge rather than assume it: run the equivalence probe and one quality benchmark on merged vs unmerged, once. Record the delta. If it exceeds the measured band, serve unmerged and let the multi-LoRA subtree run instead.

merge_verification.compare: merged vs unmerged, same seed, same prompts
merge_verification.accept: divergence within the measured band AND quality delta within its confidence interval
merge_verification.on_fail: serve unmerged; enable the multi_lora subtree; report the merge delta to the user
merge_verification.note: Two launches in stage 0, not stage 2 -- it gates whether the rest of the run even applies. Charged to stage 1's budget.
